messages.content: Now that Denver is behind me, can you help me start the D.C. MLK weekend? Tentatively fly Atlanta to Washington on Saturday, January 17, and come back Monday the 19th. It would be me, Arjun, and Leela, mostly museums.

Absolutely. For a short museum weekend, the big choices are airport convenience, hotel neighborhood, and whether Friday night is realistic. Before I narrow: are you thinking carry-ons only, and is there a rough hotel budget ceiling?

Probably carry-ons. No firm budget yet, but I don't want to spend silly money for two nights. I would rather have a well-rated place near Metro and museums. Breakfast included would be nice, but not if it pushes us way out.

That points first to DCA plus a central hotel. DCA is the easiest airport for the Mall; BWI can be cheaper but adds rail/rideshare time, and IAD is usually the least useful for this specific weekend. For hotels, I would compare National Mall/L'Enfant, Penn Quarter/Metro Center, and one roomier suite option farther out with breakfast.
Can you sketch those neighborhoods before we get into exact hotels?

Sure. National Mall/L'Enfant is the simplest for Smithsonian days and quick breaks, but breakfast is often paid and rates run higher. Penn Quarter/Metro Center has better dinner options and easy Metro, with a slightly longer walk to some museums. Navy Yard, NoMa, or Capitol Hill suite hotels may include breakfast and give more space, but you trade 15-25 minutes each way on Metro.
What about Arlington or Rosslyn? I saw a few decent rates there last time I looked.

Rosslyn can work if the rate is meaningfully better: easy Metro, quick rideshare from DCA, and some dining. The drawback is that every museum visit starts with a river crossing, so it is less low-friction than staying near the Mall for only two nights.
DCA versus BWI is probably the debate. My spouse will notice if BWI is cheaper.

For three people, I would only push BWI if it saves roughly $180-$250 total after ground transport. Otherwise DCA is worth the premium because it saves time on both ends and keeps Monday simpler before the flight home.
There is still a chance we could leave Friday evening. Does that change things?

Only if you can leave early enough to reach the hotel by about 9:30 PM. A late Friday flight plus an extra hotel night mostly buys you a less rushed Saturday morning. If school release or work makes Friday late, Saturday morning nonstop into DCA is cleaner.
Got it. What do I need to ask Arjun before we narrow it?

Ask him these: can Friday actually work, and what is the latest hotel arrival he would tolerate; how much extra DCA is worth over BWI; a target nightly hotel budget including taxes; whether a standard two-queen room is fine or if you want a suite; which museum is the must-do timed-entry one; and whether breakfast is a requirement or just a nice-to-have. In the meantime, I’ll build a Saturday-to-Monday shortlist around DCA, 4.0-plus guest ratings, Metro access, and a farther-out breakfast-included option only if the savings are compelling.

messages.content: Update on D.C.: Friday is out. No early school release, and Arjun can't leave before late afternoon anyway. Let's compare the strongest Saturday-to-Monday options.

Good, then I would drop the Friday idea. The strongest plan is Saturday morning ATL-DCA nonstop and Monday afternoon DCA-ATL nonstop. The main hotel decision is location versus breakfast/space: a Mall-adjacent hotel with paid breakfast, or a suite hotel with included breakfast farther from the museums.
Please include the BWI cheaper option just so I can defend not picking it.

Here are the three realistic packages: 1) DCA convenience: Delta nonstop ATL-DCA about 8:25 AM-10:05 AM, Monday return about 4:35 PM-6:28 PM, Holiday Inn Washington Capitol/National Mall, around 4.2 Google rating, paid breakfast. 2) DCA plus breakfast: same flights, Residence Inn Capitol Hill/Navy Yard, around 4.4 rating, suite and included breakfast, but more Metro time. 3) BWI savings: cheaper nonstop into BWI, but longer transfer and less pleasant Monday logistics.
How much cheaper is BWI in the version you see?

Roughly $210 less in airfare for all three, but you give back about $90-$130 in rail or rideshare costs and add about 1.5 to 2.5 total hours across the weekend. Net savings may be only $80-$120. For a two-night museum trip, I would keep DCA.
What if we take the cheaper Monday midday flight back from DCA?

The midday DCA return saves about $45 per person, so around $135 total. The tradeoff is big: you would need to leave the hotel area around 9:45 or 10:00 AM, which effectively kills a final museum visit. The afternoon return gives you a real Monday morning in D.C.
Okay. Walk me through the hotel math. Breakfast is my hang-up.

Mall option: Holiday Inn Washington Capitol/National Mall, standard two-queen room, roughly $248 per night before taxes, breakfast not included. Estimate two nights all-in around $590, plus simple breakfasts around $70-$90 total if you use nearby quick options. Suite option: Residence Inn Capitol Hill/Navy Yard, about $214 per night before taxes, breakfast included, all-in roughly $510. So the Mall option is about $150-$170 more after breakfast.
How much more convenient is the Mall hotel really?

Meaningfully more convenient. From the Mall hotel you can walk to Air and Space, Natural History, American History, and L'Enfant Plaza Metro, and you can drop back for coats or a break. From Navy Yard, the Metro ride is not hard, but in January rain or cold it adds planning and station time every outing.
Any dining issue around the Mall hotel?

No major issue. It has on-site food, and there are casual dinner choices around L'Enfant, the Wharf, and Penn Quarter. The Wharf is a short rideshare or a longer walk depending on weather. The suite hotel has good Navy Yard dining too, but it is less central for museum breaks.
Can you put the final two side by side with the afternoon return only?

With the afternoon return: Mall hotel package costs more, has paid breakfast and a standard room, but wins on walking access, easy luggage drop, and less transit. Suite hotel package saves about $160 total, includes breakfast, and gives more room, but adds Metro time and makes midday rests less likely. Since this is only two nights and museum-heavy, I recommend the Mall hotel.
Let's do DCA, afternoon return, and the Mall hotel. Main cabin, not basic. Can we get adjacent seats with me by a window if possible?

Yes. The main cabin fare has seat selection. Outbound has 22A, 22B, and 22C together, so you can take the window. Return has 24D, 24E, and 24F together, with 24F as your window. I would avoid the cheaper basic fare because it risks splitting the seats.
Book it with a refundable hotel rate, please.

Booked: Delta main cabin ATL-DCA Saturday, January 17, 8:25 AM-10:05 AM, and DCA-ATL Monday, January 19, 4:35 PM-6:28 PM. Seats selected together: 22A-C outbound and 24D-F return, with you at the window. Hotel booked refundable: Holiday Inn Washington Capitol/National Mall, two queen room, Saturday and Sunday nights. Breakfast is not included.
Anything I should tell Arjun besides the breakfast not being included?

Tell him the DCA choice avoids most of the BWI ground-time penalty, the afternoon return preserves a final museum morning, and the hotel location is the reason we accepted paid breakfast. Last caveats: reserve the timed-entry museum as soon as you decide which one, budget roughly $70-$90 for two simple breakfasts, and plan to drop bags if the room is not ready when you arrive Saturday.

messages.content: Can you give me the final D.C. family checklist? Flights and hotel are set. I saw cold rain may hit Sunday, and I still haven't dealt with the timed-entry museum.

Yes. For the 8:25 AM ATL-DCA flight, aim to be inside ATL by about 6:40 AM; leaving Decatur around 5:55-6:05 should give you cushion. Check in exactly when Delta opens it, download boarding passes, and do a same-morning flight-status check before leaving.
We are carry-on only. What is the easiest DCA-to-hotel plan?

Take Metro if everyone is in good shape with bags: Yellow Line from DCA to L'Enfant Plaza is usually the simplest, then a short walk to the hotel. If it is raining hard or the child is tired, rideshare is the easier backup.
The room may not be ready when we arrive. I don't want to wander with bags.

Go straight to the hotel, drop carry-ons with the front desk or bell storage, and keep one small daypack with chargers, snacks, gloves, and any museum items. Ask them to text when the room is ready, then start with lunch or a nearby Smithsonian.
Breakfast is still not included, correct?

Correct. Use the hotel cafe only if it is convenient; otherwise plan quick breakfasts near L'Enfant or the Smithsonian area. Budget about $35-$45 per morning for simple coffee, pastries, or sandwiches for the three of you.
Which timed entry should I handle now, and can you check seats one more time?

Reserve Air and Space timed entry now, ideally Saturday afternoon or Monday late morning. Keep Sunday as the flexible rainy-day indoor block: Natural History, American History, National Gallery, or Spy Museum if you want a paid backup. Seats are still together: 22A-C outbound and 24D-F return, with window seats for you. No better adjacent window row is open; recheck at check-in, but do not give up the three seats together.
